item.title: New SCP idea in need of greenlighting
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror/Mystery

Page Layout (Optional): Standard layout with the new ACS + incident reports, interview logs, recovery log, etc.

Elevator Pitch: Short pitch: It's a sentient toy troll that can move and talk that carries a mycotoxin that, when inhaled, makes the subject turn into a mindless zombie covered in hair. The mindless zombie covered in hair will attempt to hug any human close to it, which will spread the infection.

+ Longer pitch
- Longer pitch

This SCP is a Euclid class anomaly. It is a sentient toy resembling Fuzzbert, a character from the Trolls movie. It is capable of movement and speech, although its speech has to be translated using an unknown device. When it is disturbed or feels endangered it lets out a mycotoxin (SCP-XXXX-1) that, when inhaled by a human or any other living organism in the class Mammalia, attacks the brain causing growth hormone modifications, which results in accelerated hair growth starting from the subjects head and ending around its pelvic region. Hair growth can also be seen from the subject's eyes, nostrils, ears, mouth, and below the fingernails. After a certain amount of time, the subjects (now referred to as SCP-XXXX-2) cognitive functions will become limited and it will attempt to hug any human it comes in contact with, which will result in the infection spreading to that person. SCP-XXXX-2 instances mainly show interest in humans, but other living organisms in the class Mammalia that come in contact with it will develop the same symptoms.

Central Narrative: On January 8. 2009. a boy was playing near an old Russian nuclear power plant when he found a weird toy that started walking towards him making weird gurgling noises. The boy got very curious and decided to pick the toy up. The toy started shaking and let out a cloud of green mist. The boy got scared and ran home, taking the toy with him. After a few minutes, he started having flu-like symptoms, with tingling sensations around his nose. He started growing massive amounts of hair around his body and started attacking his own mother. Obviously scared, she called the police. The police arrived shortly after and found a creature covered in hair trying to break into a room. They neutralized the creature and contacted the SCP Foundation shortly after. When the Foundation arrived, they found a small toy that was walking around the house. They figured that that toy was the cause of the incident. They immediately sedated it and transported it to Site-██, where it currently resides. It was classified as a Euclid level SCP and given the number XXXX.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: I feel like this SCP is a mix of multiple other existing SCPs but still has originality. It is interesting how mysterious its origin is, no one currently knows how it came to be or why it infects people, or how it can communicate with other people, or why instances of SCP-XXXX-2 are only interested in humans but can infect other animals as well. But those questions might be answered in the future… I also feel like the symptoms of the infection are pretty interesting, with all the hair growth and trying to hug people.

Additional Notes: So I already made a sandbox article, but I still think it needs some working to be done on it. Also, I was thinking of slowly answering all the questions about the SCP through interview logs and stuff, and also doing some SCP cross-links if you're ok with it. I will post the draft link here if you want.

item.title: New SCP Idea
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): Containment procedures, description, an addendum or two, and 2 ethics committee reports

Elevator Pitch: A man with severely burned skin who claims to have gone to the Christian hell. His skin will anomalously smolder and catch on fire at random intervals.

Central Narrative: One day, a man drenched in fire ran out of a burning building. It took a while to put him out and calm him down, but it was a mystery as to how he survived. The Foundation was alerted when his burns refused to heal and even got hotter, sometimes causing fires.

The man claimed to be Junior Toure, an Angolan man who died 67 years before he was found by The Foundation. His skin stayed burned and caught on fire randomly, but that was easily dealt with in the form of automatic sprinklers.

The man claimed to have gone to what he believed to be the Christian interpretation of hell, claiming to have seen glimpses of an endless field with people laying on the ground, bound by chains, forever on fire, the flames growing ever hotter.

He was in constant pain. He cried regularly and screams could be heard from his cell for hours on end. There was no way to help him. Eventually, a grievance with the ethics committee was filed, asking them if he should be put out of his misery. After an interview, he said "I don't want that. I don't want to return."

+ show block
– hide block

Toure aged normally, and as he did, his mental state deteriorated. He became paranoid and erratic, fearing death and a return to that hellish place. He died insane, with the only resemblance of peace being him requesting that his body be put in the ocean, saying "It might dull the pain while I'm down there."

His body burned nonstop after he died, with nothing being able to stop it. It eventually turned into a pile of ash. Another ethics committee grievance was filed, asking for Toure's last wish to be granted. The committee stipulated that if the ash had no anomalous properties, then it was to be dispersed in the Pacific Ocean.

The ash was found to be non-anomalous, and the dead man's wish was fulfilled. His ashes found their way to the bottom of the ocean, bearing a stark contrast to what he was bound to for eternity to come.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's a very dark SCP, which is nothing new, but it would also be a neutralized SCP.

Additional Notes:


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

item.title: Forum Criticism Team - Captain Post
item.content:encoded:
Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea: A Motel With An Elevator
item.content:encoded:
I enjoy anomalies that are weird, wrong buildings like this one and SCP-455. However, you will need to do something to make yours stand out from the already very large number of anomalies that are weird buildings full of weird things with weird exploration logs. Perhaps create some sort of narrative, something that ties together these hotel rooms as something other than random weird shit. Is some entity collecting samples of other universes? Is this a secret wing of the hotel that caters to beings from other realities? Are the things inside related to the person doing the exploring? How can the Foundation utilize this anomaly? You needn’t answer these questions necessarily, but I do recommend including some mystery about the anomaly’s purpose or nature and either implying the solution or revealing it in the exploration logs.

Addressing a few things:

+ show block
– hide block

But that's not what's happening here.

We're here debating matters of fact. Who does and does not go on death row.

Some of the things I'd want to ask in workshop are where have these concepts been tried before, what worked and what didn't? Is any part of the concept in direct contradiction of cannon?

D-Class portrayal is a rather significant part of the Foundation Universe canon at large (the site even had a contest focusing on D-Class: http://www.scpwiki.com/d-class-contest). If you really want to have your core anomaly be frivolously exposed to multiple anomalies in order to ensure your planned plotline happens, you do so at the risk of readers becoming skeptical of Foundation incompetence.

If this discussion is a workshop then I'm 100% on board.

I'll be honest, thus far it doesn't look like you're open to adjusting anything but the smallest details of your concept. That combined with what seems to be an insinuation that the discussion doesn't meet your standards for "a workshop" and thus it's the reviewers' fault for you not editing your concept doesn't really encourage readers to want to assist you.

It's fine if you want to write material solely based on your interests in "fleshing out the canon" with minimal edits—those works are posted to the Fan Work forum and are not expected to be closely critiqued (if at all).

If you want to post content to the mainsite where it will be voted on by readers who have their own headcanon that may not mesh with your own, you're going to need to adjust your premise rather than trying to convince readers that they need to change their preferences to suit yours. The large majority of our day-to-day readers/voters read for leisure and don't check author posts; your content needs to be compelling without needing you to defend it in several separate discussion posts.

Against their will.

If, as Zyn proposes, a murderer from the US is deemed too sadistic to work with, would the alternative be an illiterate goat-heard from Saudi Arabia who's been convicted of adultery and speaks no english?

Are there an infinite number of these people, or do compromises ever have to be made?

I ask these questions not to be argumentative, but because these are interesting problems. There are probably several interesting stories here. Opportunities to flesh out the cannon.

This interests me. It's stories like this I want to work on.

Part of the greenlight/crit process is to not only help you flesh out your idea/draft, but to also help guide new authors to stuff that works on the site.

But that's not what's happening here.

We're here debating matters of fact. Who does and does not go on death row.

Help fleshing it out would be great.

I often tend to think that being willing to adjust an idea in workshop is preferable to having your piece get downvoted to oblivion on the main site.

Totally agree. If this discussion is a workshop then I'm 100% on board.

Some of the things I'd want to ask in workshop are where have these concepts been tried before, what worked and what didn't? Is any part of the concept in direct contradiction of cannon? How does a Scranton Reality Anchor work? Were it done to death or was absolutely impossible for some reason of established cannon, I would drop it or adjust.

My opinions about the kinds of problems I'm interested in probably won't change, but there are many angles from which to attack them. I'd find another.

Finally, I strongly urge you to read the more recent articles on the site to draw inspiration from.

This I am doing.

(Terrible for climate change if civilians heard about the transformed skip; great for Mideast diplomacy and Broken God proselytizers.)

item.title: Re: Anomalous-D
item.content:encoded:
As a practical matter in the US,

Why the hell would the Foundation use only US death row prisoners? That's absolutely idiotic.

First of all, death row prisoners in places like China, Iran, and Saudi Arabia, at least cumulatively, far outnumber those in the United States.

Additionally, few people are as closely tracked as US Death Row prisoners. Many are causes célèbre for anti-execution campaigners (groups that are much larger and more vocal in the United States due to the relative political freedom compared to other countries which execute). Why would you go with exclusively United States prisoners, who must be made to disappear and are far smaller in number, when you can get far greater numbers with far less effort abroad?

Do some research before you argue a point.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Anomalous-D

item.title: Re: Anomalous-D
item.content:encoded:
Not all D-class come from "death row". Not all D-class come from the United States. The SCP Foundation is a global organization that pulls staff from all corners of the globe and beyond. Fixating exclusively on how the US does things is unhelpful and not relevant in this context.

Murdermachine SCPs were a staple in earlier forms of the wiki and have more or less dropped off in popularity, despite the prevalence of them in off-site media. The reality is is that they've been done over and over again and the concept is now worn out and boring.

The entire concept is relying heavily on decade old material and doesn't reflect the current atmosphere or environment of the wiki. Part of the greenlight/crit process is to not only help you flesh out your idea/draft, but to also help guide new authors to stuff that works on the site. You can either listen to this advice, or post your thing anyway and let the voting populace decide.

I often tend to think that being willing to adjust an idea in workshop is preferable to having your piece get downvoted to oblivion on the main site.

Finally, I strongly urge you to read the more recent articles on the site to draw inspiration from. A lot of the series-1 articles have been replicated so many times now that people are simply sick of it. Utilizing them as the primary foci of a current piece rarely does well.

item.title: Re: the cup
item.content:encoded:
This concept has potential, as you said though it does bear an extreme resemblance to SCP 294. It needs some more development.

An idea that popped into my head was deviating from SCP 294 by making it not useful. Maybe the liquid manifests inside every cup in a building. It's cool at first, but then the inhabitants begin realizing they cant get rid of it and are stuck with that drink. If they pour the liquid out in the sink and go to the coffee machine to pour some coffee, they look back down to see the cup is filled with sprite again. They look back up to see the coffee machine is also now filled with sprite. Eventually it begins coming out of the faucets. The gas tank of every car in the parking lot is filled with it too. The lake nearby is entirely composed of it as well. There's no escape from the favorite drink until the scp is somehow removed.

That's just one direction you could take it, but try coming up with more, theres tons of possibilities
